+# ZIP archival (current format)
+
+Each cover ID is a decimal number padded to exactly 10 digits. The first four digits identify an archive.org item (1,000,000 covers); the next two identify a ZIP batch (10,000 covers). For example, cover `8010042` is `0008010042` in item `covers_0008`, batch `01`. Each size has its own item and ZIP:
+
+| Size | Item | ZIP path under `data_root` | Image inside ZIP |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Original | `covers_0008` | `items/covers_0008/covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042.jpg` |
+| Small | `s_covers_0008` | `items/s_covers_0008/s_covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042-S.jpg` |
+| Medium | `m_covers_0008` | `items/m_covers_0008/m_covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042-M.jpg` |
+| Large | `l_covers_0008` | `items/l_covers_0008/l_covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042-L.jpg` |
+
+The URL is `https://archive.org/download/<item>/<zip>/<image>`. ZIP entries are stored without compression for direct remote access. `archive.archive(test=False)` stages images and marks records `archived`; local originals remain readable. `Batch(8, 1).process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True, test=False)` uploads any missing ZIPs, checks `ia list` for every ZIP, then replaces `filename*` with download URLs, sets `uploaded`, and removes verified staged and local files. A failed verification leaves the batch staged for retry. Covers with missing local source images are marked `failed=true` and excluded from subsequent archival runs until repaired. A per-batch file lock serializes local archival and finalization runs. The lock assumes all workers share `data_root`.
+
+Existing databases need `failed boolean default false` and `uploaded boolean default false` on `cover`, plus indexes `cover_failed_idx` and `cover_uploaded_idx`; the new schema includes them. Older tar records remain readable through the legacy tar reader. The historical notes below describe the older tar process.

+# ZIP archival (current format)
+
+Each cover ID is a decimal number padded to exactly 10 digits. The first four digits identify an archive.org item (1,000,000 covers); the next two identify a ZIP batch (10,000 covers). For example, cover `8010042` is `0008010042` in item `covers_0008`, batch `01`. Each size has its own item and ZIP:
+
+| Size | Item | ZIP path under `data_root` | Image inside ZIP |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Original | `covers_0008` | `items/covers_0008/covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042.jpg` |
+| Small | `s_covers_0008` | `items/s_covers_0008/s_covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042-S.jpg` |
+| Medium | `m_covers_0008` | `items/m_covers_0008/m_covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042-M.jpg` |
+| Large | `l_covers_0008` | `items/l_covers_0008/l_covers_0008_01.zip` | `0008010042-L.jpg` |
+
+The URL is `https://archive.org/download/<item>/<zip>/<image>`. ZIP entries are stored without compression for direct remote access. `archive.archive(test=False)` stages images and marks records `archived`; local originals remain readable. `Batch(8, 1).process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True, test=False)` uploads any missing ZIPs, checks `ia list` for every ZIP, then replaces `filename*` with download URLs, sets `uploaded`, and removes verified staged and local files. A failed verification leaves the batch staged for retry. Covers with missing local source images are marked `failed=true` and excluded from subsequent archival runs until repaired. A per-batch file lock serializes local archival and finalization runs. The lock assumes all workers share `data_root`.
+
+Existing databases need `failed boolean default false` and `uploaded boolean default false` on `cover`, plus indexes `cover_failed_idx` and `cover_uploaded_idx`; the new schema includes them. Older tar records remain readable through the legacy tar reader. The historical notes below describe the older tar process.
